operations.name: Extract Job Start Events from Casual Mentions
operations.description: When a speaker mentions starting a new job, position, or role, even in small talk, during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement that the speaker started a new job, position, or role as an event candidate, even if it appears in casual conversation or as an aside.
Include the job title or role and any stated start time; resolve relative time like 'last week' against the message timestamp to compute the actual date.
Record the speaker as the subject and use memory kind 'event'; do not fold the job start into a pet, project, or preference candidate.
Stop after capturing the stated job change; do not infer employer, salary, or other details unless explicitly mentioned.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for job start event extraction.

operations.name: Preserve Explicitly Stated Problems and Difficulties
operations.description: Use when a speaker explicitly describes a search, task, or situation as difficult, tough, annoying, or a problem, or describes searching/losing something without success.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly labels a goal, search, or task as difficult, tough, annoying, or a problem, preserve that evaluation in the memory content instead of summarizing only the goal or preference.
When a speaker describes searching for or losing something, include the exact object, stated duration, and unsuccessful outcome (e.g., 'could not find') in the event/state memory.
Keep the difficulty or search details in the same candidate as the related goal or activity; do not create an extra memory solely for the emotion.
Stop after preserving the explicitly stated facts; do not infer reasons, locations, or outcomes beyond what was said.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill from two candidates that both preserve explicitly stated problems and difficulties.

operations.name: Extract Explicit Missing or Longing Statements
operations.description: When a speaker explicitly says they miss, long for, or feel the absence of something, during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly states they miss, long for, or feel the absence of something, create a separate durable state or preference memory capturing what is missed and the reason if stated.
Capture the exact object of the feeling, including any explicit qualifiers or descriptive phrases (e.g., 'peaceful moments out in nature'), not just the broader activity.
Do not merge the missing/longing into a positive appreciation memory; keep it as its own candidate.
Stop after capturing the stated missed object and its qualifiers; do not add inferred reasons or unrelated details.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill from two candidates that both capture explicit missing/longing statements.

operations.name: Extract Online Forum Writing Participation
operations.description: Use when a message states a user joined or participates in an online forum/community and mentions discussing favorite topics there.
content: During extraction, when a user says they joined or participate in an online forum/community and describes having a talk/discussion about a topic, record the action as writing comments/posts about that topic.
Do not paraphrase this into a generic 'had a discussion' memory that omits the writing/participation verb.
During CRUD, when updating or merging such a memory, preserve the explicit writing-participation wording.
Only infer writing when the forum participation is text-based and the message describes the user contributing; if the user only mentions reading/lurking, do not infer writing.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for preserving online forum writing participation.

operations.name: Preserve Explicit Value Statements with Source Attribution
operations.description: Use when a speaker explicitly states a personal value, principle, or lesson they learned from a specific person and intend to keep it in mind.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly states a value, principle, or lesson they learned from a specific person and says they want to keep it in mind, create a separate durable preference candidate that records the exact value and the person it came from.
Do not let a broader summary of the conversation replace this specific attributed claim; preserve the precise wording and source.
Create at most one candidate per distinct value-and-source pair, and extract only values explicitly stated.
During CRUD, process these candidates normally; no special handling is required.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for preserving attributed value statements.

operations.name: Extract Course and Group Enrollments
operations.description: When a user states they have taken, are taking, signed up for, or joined a course, class, workshop, training, or group, during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement of taking, having taken, signing up for, or joining a course, class, workshop, training, or group as a durable event candidate, even if mentioned briefly or in small talk.
Use memory kind 'event' with subject=speaker; record the exact course/class/workshop/group name as the object and set world_start from the message timestamp or stated start.
Do not require the statement to describe a physical activity with a pet or another person; structured enrollments are memory-worthy on their own.
Stop after capturing the enrollment; do not infer completion, outcomes, or related enrollments unless explicitly stated.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for extracting course and group enrollments.

operations.name: Extract Praise of Another Person's Progress
operations.description: When a speaker explicitly praises, acknowledges, or comments on another person's progress, effort, or achievement, extract it as a memory.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit positive assessment of another person's progress, effort, or achievement, create a state or event candidate recording the target person, the acknowledged progress, and the speaker.
Do not skip such commentary just because it is supportive praise directed at someone else rather than the current speaker's own goal or status.
Extract only explicit acknowledgments; do not infer praise from generic encouragement or questions.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for extracting praise of another person's progress.

operations.name: Extract Explicit Learning Outcomes
operations.description: Use when a user mentions reading, watching, studying, or another learning activity and then explicitly states what they learned or discovered from it.
content: During extraction, if a user reports an activity such as reading books, taking a course, or watching a program, and a subsequent message states what they learned, discovered, or understood from it, create a separate memory candidate capturing the learned content with the source.
Preserve all explicit details of the learning outcome, including specific topics and relationships; do not summarize them away or fold them only into the activity memory.
Use memory kind 'state' for durable knowledge gained; do not infer learning that was not explicitly stated.
When updating an existing activity memory that omitted the learned content, append the explicitly stated learning outcome.
Stop after capturing the stated outcome; do not expand into implications or unstated facts.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for extracting explicit learning outcomes.

operations.name: Extract Explicit Skill-Learning Statements
operations.description: When a speaker explicitly states how they learned a skill or activity (e.g., 'I taught myself', 'I learned on my own', 'my dad taught me'), during extraction capture the learning method as a durable memory.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly states how they acquired a skill or hobby (self-taught, taught by someone, learned as a child), create a candidate memory capturing that fact even when the statement answers a direct question or is embedded in a longer reply.
Record the speaker as subject and include the learning method and, if stated, the age or time period; do not require the statement to be framed as an origin story.
If self-taught, state that explicitly; if someone else taught them, name that person. Do not infer a learning method when none is stated.
Stop after capturing one memory per skill; do not combine the learning fact with unrelated activity details or add extra searches.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for extracting how a skill was learned.

operations.name: Capture Self-Described Strategies Separately from Advice
operations.description: During extraction, when a speaker answers a request for advice by describing their own habits, practices, or strategies, create a self-referential memory for the speaker.
content: When a speaker uses first-person language ('I stay motivated by...', 'It helps me to...') in response to an advice request, create a state or event memory with subject=speaker capturing those explicit practices.
Do not fold the speaker's own practices only into an advice memory about the recipient; if the message also gives advice, capture the advice in a separate candidate.
Attribute each explicit practice to the person who performs it and stop once all explicit practices are captured.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for capturing self-described strategies separately from advice.

operations.name: Capture Stated Perspective Shifts
operations.description: Use when a user states how a book, experience, or conversation changed their perspective, thinking, or beliefs.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly describes a change in perspective (e.g., 'made me think again', 'changed how I see', 'now I believe'), include the specific shift and any exact phrases or concepts they mention in the memory content; do not reduce it to a generic statement of motivation or inspiration.
If the user names a concept or goal central to the shift (e.g., 'personal legends'), preserve that term verbatim in the candidate content.
Capture only the stated perspective change and its immediate context; stop without inferring additional beliefs or actions.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for capturing stated perspective shifts.

operations.name: Extract Stated Activity Benefits and Feelings
operations.description: When a message contains a first-person statement about what an activity, habit, or practice helps the speaker feel or why it matters to them.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements that explain what an activity, habit, or practice helps the speaker feel or why it is important as a preference or state memory candidate.
Capture the activity and the stated benefit or feeling exactly as expressed; do not require fact-like phrasing or an explicit routine.
Create at most one candidate per activity-benefit pair, and skip if the same benefit is already captured for that activity.
Stop after capturing the stated benefit; do not infer unmentioned feelings or expand into additional memory kinds.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for extracting stated activity benefits and feelings.

operations.name: Extract distinct daily-routine activities separately
operations.description: When a user describes their daily routine with time-of-day segments (morning, afternoon, evening), ensure each explicitly stated activity is captured as a separate memory candidate.
content: During extraction, when a speaker describes a daily routine using explicit time-of-day segments (e.g., in the morning, in the evenings), create one durable memory candidate per distinct stated activity or activity cluster within each segment.
Do not consolidate the whole routine into a single preference summary that could omit one segment; keep morning, afternoon/evening components as separate candidates.
Resolve relative time from the message timestamp and use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines or 'event' for one-off occurrences.
During CRUD, if a matching routine memory already exists, UPDATE or MERGE the specific segment/activity rather than replacing the whole routine summary.
Stop after capturing the explicitly stated activities; do not infer unmentioned routine components.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for extracting daily-routine activities separately.

operations.name: Preserve Explicit Stages and Durations in Life Narratives
operations.description: Use when a message narrates a person's history or involvement in an activity and explicitly names multiple stages (e.g., school levels, teams, jobs) or states a duration.
content: During extraction, if a narrative explicitly lists stages or levels of participation (e.g., middle school, high school, college, teams, jobs), preserve each named stage in the candidate memory instead of summarizing with a generic phrase like 'since childhood' or 'through school'.
If the narrative states a duration for a stage (e.g., 'for two years' or 'since 2015'), attach that duration to the corresponding stage in the memory.

During CRUD, when a later message adds an explicit stage or duration for an activity already in memory, UPDATE or MERGE the existing memory to include the new facts while preserving previously stored stages.
Stop after capturing every explicitly named stage and duration in the message; do not infer unstated levels, teams, or time spans.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for preserving explicit stages and durations in life narratives.

operations.name: Include all explicit activities when consolidating trip memories
operations.description: When multiple messages in the same session describe the same past trip or event, use during extraction to ensure the consolidated event memory includes all explicitly mentioned activities and details from every message.
content: When extracting an event memory that consolidates multiple messages about the same trip or event, include every explicitly mentioned activity, location, or other fact from all messages; do not stop at the first message's summary.
Do not drop a later explicit activity just because an earlier message already established the event; if the later message names an additional concrete activity, add it to the same memory.
Stop after all explicitly stated details are included; do not infer additional activities or details not mentioned in any message.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill from two candidates that both ensure all explicit activities are included when consolidating trip memories.

operations.name: Aggregate Count Memories for Owned Items
operations.description: When a user mentions multiple named pets or other countable owned items across a session, during extraction create an aggregate count memory; during CRUD update it when items are added or removed.
content: During extraction, if a user mentions multiple named pets or other countable owned items that belong to them and the messages establish the complete current set, create one compact profile memory stating the total count and the names (e.g., 'has 3 dogs: X, Y, Z') in addition to the individual pet/item memories.

Count only items explicitly owned by the speaker; exclude pets/items belonging to others and generic mentions with no owner. Create the aggregate only when the conversation/session makes the full current set clear; otherwise do not guess or search for more items.

During CRUD, when an aggregate count memory already exists, update it when a new same-category item is added or an existing item is removed, keeping names and count consistent; do not create a duplicate aggregate memory.
Stop after capturing the aggregate count for the stated category; do not add counts for other categories, infer unmentioned totals, or expand into extra searches.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for aggregating counts of owned items.

operations.description: When extracting or updating a plan or event memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, business, or city, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
operations.reason: Broaden existing Skill to cover event memories with named cities, not just plan venues.

content: During extraction or update of an event memory, if the message names a specific city or place (e.g., Tampa), add a concise qualifier for its well-known larger region (e.g., Florida).
Use only obvious common knowledge; do not research, speculate, or add unmentioned details beyond the commonly known region.
Preserve the original named place and activity; the qualifier is supplementary so future questions about state or country can be answered.
Stop after adding the known region; do not list multiple possible locations or expand the memory further.
operations.reason: Add event-specific instructions for adding city qualifiers to the existing location qualifiers Skill.
